subject: Acme reliability review: mitigation track, timeline and handoffs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sana Rao <sana@acme.com>, ops+oncall@acme.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme reliability review: mitigation track, timeline and handoffs

Hi Sana —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Per our call, attaching a concise pack that summarizes the outage timeline and a short, prioritized mitigation track with clear owners and target dates. High-level summary:

- What happened: a regression in request routing logic combined with a KV-cache invalidation race caused increased tail latency for a subset of inference requests (~0.6% of traffic) between 02:40–03:05 UTC.
- Immediate impact: increased 504s and retries for several Acme production routes; no data exfiltration.
- Customer-visible: order confirmation flow slowed for ~3% of users during the window; you already saw the retry bursts.

Attached: acme_incident_timeline_20270528.pdf (2 pages) and a CSV that maps mitigation owners to tasks (mitigation-track-owners.csv).

Proposed mitigation track (short):
1) Short-term (48h): enable conservative routing fallback to v1 model binary + tighten KV cache TTLs — owner: Marissa Cole — target: 2027-05-30 EOD.
2) Mid-term (2 weeks): backfill additional routing unit tests, add end-to-end guard for cache invalidation — owner: Connor O'Brien — target: 2027-06-11.
3) Long-term (quarter): workflow for rollout window detection + automated canary rollbacks — owner: Laura Bennett — target: 2027-08-01.

Ask: Please confirm Acme is comfortable with these owners and timelines or flag a date constraint you need us to meet. If you prefer an on-call walk-through of the fallback toggle we can do that today.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0128
[Attachment: acme_incident_timeline_20270528.pdf] [Attachment: mitigation-track-owners.csv]

From: Sana Rao <sana@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+oncall@acme.com, procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme reliability review: mitigation track, timeline and handoffs

Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear owners. A couple of clarifying questions before we sign off on the timelines:

1) For the short-term fallback to v1, what is the expected client-visible latency delta? We need to set expectations with our product leads.
2) For the 48h window, can you commit to a drill run for the fallback toggle so our on-call engineers are comfortable executing it?

Our priority is minimizing user impact during peak checkout windows next week (UTC 17:00–20:00). If Marissa can schedule the drill before next Thu that would be ideal. Also looping in procurement because we may ask for a nominal SLA credit while remediation is in progress.

Thanks,
Sana
Sana Rao
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Commerce
sana@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sana Rao <sana@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme reliability review: mitigation track, timeline and handoffs

Thanks, Sana — quick responses inline.

> 1) For the short-term fallback to v1, what is the expected client-visible latency delta?

Short answer: 120–200ms increase on median for the affected routes; worst-case 400ms during bursty retries. That is based on our internal perf runs comparing v1 vs v2 binaries in your approximate request size distribution. I'll paste the brief microbench numbers into the shared doc.

> 2) For the 48h window, can you commit to a drill run for the fallback toggle so our on-call engineers are comfortable executing it?

Yes — I can run the drill. Proposed slot: Mon 2027-05-31 16:00 UTC (which is your evening peak start) — it's a low-risk dry-run using a canary subset. If that works, Connor will prepare the runbook and I'll send a step-by-step with the rollback checklist.

Action items I'm locking in now (also added to mitigation-track-owners.csv):
- Marissa: schedule and run fallback drill, publish runbook (owner: marissa_cole) — target: 2027-05-31 16:00 UTC.
- Connor: unit & e2e test additions; cache invalidation guard (owner: connor_obrien) — target: 2027-06-11.
- Laura: rollout policy + automated canary rollback spec (owner: laura_bennett) — target: 2027-08-01.
- Ben: coordinate commercial note on SLA credit request and customer comms (owner: ben_carter) — target: 2027-05-31 close.

Sana — once you confirm the drill slot I'll create a calendar invite with dial-in + readout notes.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sana Rao <sana@acme.com>, ops+oncall@acme.com, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme reliability review: mitigation track, timeline and handoffs

Sana — thanks for the quick confirm.

We'll proceed as follows:
- Drill scheduled: Mon 2027-05-31 16:00 UTC (calendar invite sent).
- Marissa will lead drill; Connor to provide runbook and test artifacts by EOD Mon.
- I'll open the SLA credit request and follow up with procurement privately; our finance/sales ops contact is cc'd on the procurement thread.
- Laura will publish the rollout spec doc to the link below and include rollback KPIs.

Customer-facing summary (what we will share to customers after the drill): a two-page timeline, confirmed root cause, the short/mid/long mitigation track with owners and delivery windows, and a note on the SLA credit request. We aim to publish that summary by Tue 2027-06-01.

Link to working doc: https://docs.redwood.com/incident/acme/20270528/summary

If any of the timing conflicts with your schedules, flag here and we'll reprioritize. Otherwise we'll follow the mitigation track and keep you posted after the drill.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0128
